title: On-call Summary Cards & Incident Timeline Composer (postmortem auto-linking)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and prototype a compact, scannable On-call Summary Card and a linked Incident Timeline Composer inside the Redwood Console. Goals: reduce cognitive load during handoffs, surface SLO delta and cost impact next to critical alerts, and enable one-click creation/association of postmortem notes and Drive/Confluence links. The feature must work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private views and respect RBAC (only show postmortem links to allowed roles).
background: Support teams repeatedly asked for a single pane where they can: (1) see what changed to SLOs and error rates during an incident, (2) understand estimated cost delta for the incident window, and (3) create or link a postmortem without switching tools. Current console surfaces alerts and traces in separate screens which prolongs handoffs and slows post-incident workflows.
design_goals: Create a dense card that fits into the Alerts and Routes list view for quick Handoff Summary
Provide a composer that sketches the incident timeline (alerts, deployments, rollouts) with drag-to-reorder capability
Expose SLO delta and estimated cost delta for the incident window, with links to the cost breakdown page
Make postmortem creation/linking one-click: prefill title, timeframe, and attach relevant traces/PRs/dashboards
Preserve privacy and RBAC: only show 'Create postmortem' to users with incident-write rights
acceptance_criteria: On-call Summary Card is available in Alerts list as a collapsible row with: incident title, severity, affected routes, SLO delta percent, estimated cost delta (USD), top 3 active signatures (errors/latency), and a prominent 'Handoff' button.
Handoff modal opens the Incident Timeline Composer prepopulated with alert timestamps, selected traces and the last deployment event; users can add notes, reorder events, and add tags before saving.

Composer includes a 'Create postmortem' action that creates a Confluence/Drive doc stub (link returned) and attaches selected timeline events. The stub includes prefilled summary and SLO + cost snapshots.
RBAC respected: users without incident-write role see a read-only timeline and a 'Request postmortem' action which pings the on-call Slack channel with prefilled context.
Prototype validated with 3 SEs and 2 SREs in usability testing with at least 80% task completion for creating a postmortem link and summarizing SLO delta.
Telemetry events emitted: handoff_opened, timeline_saved, postmortem_created, postmortem_requested for analytics and A/B measurement.
Design handoff includes a Figma file, component specs, and CSS tokens for dark/light themes and accessibility contrast ratios.

Implementation API contract defined: composeIncidentTimeline(incident_id) returns timeline events, canPostmortem boolean, suggestedTitle string, costSnapshotUrl string. (See attachments for proposed API docs.)

implementation_notes: Frontend: reuse AlertRow component; new CompactOncallCard variant with expandable composer slot
Backend: new endpoint /incidents/{id}/compose that returns timeline events, costSnapshot and canPostmortem flag
Integration: Confluence/Drive connector uses customer's configured workspace; must check permission scopes before creating doc
Telemetry: emit events with incident_id, user_id, role, and decision tags (created|requested|attached)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cost delta calculation may be noisy for short spikes. Mitigation: show 95% confidence band and link to cost breakdown for details.
Risk: Postmortem auto-creation could leak sensitive data. Mitigation: backend generates role-limited links and requires explicit opt-in for external attachments.
Risk: Composer heaviness causing latency in alerts list. Mitigation: lazy-load composer assets and use server-side snapshots for initial render.
